subject: Request: timeboxed retention for triage — Sable Health incident
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Jansen <emily.jansen@sablehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: timeboxed retention for triage — Sable Health incident

Hi Mina / Marissa,

Sable Health is seeing a reproducing request/response mismatch that appears tied to a short-lived cache key rotation. Customer reported intermittent inference failures between 2027-04-17 23:40 and 2027-04-18 02:10 UTC. Our standard retention window has already purged some of the per-call KV cache and prefix traces that would let us verify the sequence and correlate client-side retries.

As part of triage I’m asking for a timeboxed retention exception to preserve the following artifacts for up to 72 hours (from now):
- per-request model inputs/outputs for request IDs referenced in INC-8424
- KV cache snapshots for the affected pod group
- request-level tracing headers (non-PII)

I’ve attached a small redacted log snippet showing the request IDs (support_log_snippet.txt). We will not export or share raw customer content outside the triage group, and we’ll redact any fields that look like PHI before storing longer-term. Access will be limited to: myself (diego), Marissa (CS), and one security reviewer (Mina).

Can we get a short exception (48–72 hours) to prevent deletion while we finish the root-cause analysis? If approved, I’ll update the case notes and add the HubSpot/Jira links.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com

-- Attachment: support_log_snippet.txt (text/plain)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: timeboxed retention for triage — Sable Health incident

Diego —

Thanks for the heads up and for the redacted snippet. A few clarifying items before I can approve:
1) Exact scope: provide the request ID list and the storage locations (S3 prefix / internal blob id).
2) Duration: you requested 48–72 hours. Please state the minimum required; shorter is better from a compliance perspective.
3) Access control: confirm the RBAC group that will have read access and the person responsible for deleting the snapshot after the window.
4) Data minimization: describe the redaction steps you’ll perform to remove PII/PHI. If any data is confirmed PHI we need Legal sign-off.

Assuming we can limit to non-PII request traces, I can approve a 48-hour exception scoped to the IDs you provide. If PHI risk exists, we’ll need Legal looped in from the customer side; please advise.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Emily Jansen <emily.jansen@sablehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: timeboxed retention for triage — Sable Health incident

Mina — quick answers below. I’ve also attached a text file with the Jira incident link.

1) Scope/location: INC-8424 contains the request ID list; artifacts will be staged to s3://redwood-triage/sablehealth/INC-8424/ (read-only ACL).
2) Duration: minimal requested = 48 hours. If we confirm repro and gather correlations we’ll request a one-time 24-hour extension; otherwise we delete at 48 hours.
3) Access control: RBAC group "triage-sable-INC8424" (members: diego_fernandez, marissa_cole, mina_haddad). Deletion owner: Diego Fernandez. I will run the deletion job and post the audit in Jira when complete.
4) Redaction: automated scrub removes header fields that match PII/PHI regexes; we will manually review for PHI before keeping anything beyond 48 hours. No raw storage of customer-submitted documents.

I’m happy to provide a short statement the customer can sign if Legal needs customer acknowledgement.

Diego

-- Attachment: incident-jira-link.txt (text/plain)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Emily Jansen <emily.jansen@sablehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: timeboxed retention for triage — Sable Health incident

Thanks Diego / Mina —

I’m okay with a 48-hour exception following the scope you outlined. A couple of operational asks:
- Diego, please add a single-line note to the HubSpot support case with the retention window and the RBAC group name.
- After deletion, paste the deletion audit (S3 object IDs + timestamp) back into INC-8424.

Mina: please escalate to Legal only if your review finds PHI/PHI-like fields. Otherwise, proceed with the scoped 48-hour retention.

Emily: we’ll keep this data internal to the triage group and will not surface raw payloads. If you prefer, I can provide a short statement for Sable confirming our handling and deletion timeline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Emily Jansen <emily.jansen@sablehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: timeboxed retention for triage — Sable Health incident

Marissa / Diego —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Sable Health is fine with a 48-hour timeboxed hold scoped to the IDs in INC-8424, provided Redwood confirms deletion and posts the audit in Jira. We appreciate the redaction precautions.

Emily Jansen
VP, Platform Operations
Sable Health
emily.jansen@sablehealth.com
